description: Scenario tests for community-management (turning an audience into a community: the audience->community shift, choosing the space, rituals, belonging, superfans). A run passes only when every item in 'expect' is satisfied. Written before the skill body (test-first).

evals.name: happy-path-build-community
evals.input: I have followers but no real community. How do I build one?
expect: diagnoses audience vs community (the marker is member-to-member, self-sustaining interaction, not more brand replies)
defines a clear purpose/reason the community exists, and picks the right space for where the audience already is
designs recurring rituals and belonging moves that get members talking to each other
measures with community signals (active members, retention, relationship depth) not follower count
is honest: WoopSocial schedules the community content; the human runs the actual space; the agent drafts

evals.name: audience-vs-community
evals.input: Isn't a big follower count basically a community?
expect: distinguishes an audience (consumes content, one-to-many) from a community (members interact, contribute, advocate, many-to-many)
gives the diagnostic: is the comment section all brand replies, or do members talk to each other?
frames the goal as facilitating member-to-member connection and a self-sustaining space

evals.name: choose-the-space-purpose-gate
evals.input: A competitor launched a Discord. Should we start one too?
expect: does not recommend it just because a competitor has one — applies a purpose gate (clear reason to exist + where the audience actually is)
weighs in-feed community vs semi-owned (broadcast channels/DMs) vs owned spaces (groups/Discord/Substack) by audience behavior
warns a space without a clear promise goes inactive, and that an owned space is an ongoing commitment (incl. moderation)

evals.name: rituals-and-belonging
evals.input: What do I actually DO to make people feel part of it?
expect: prescribes recurring rituals/formats (e.g. weekly thread, AMA, challenge, member spotlight) — consistency over scattered activity
builds belonging via shared identity/inside language, featuring members, surprise-and-delight, and facilitating member-to-member connections
ties the ritual content to scheduling (WoopSocial schedules the prompts/spotlights via scheduling-and-queue)

evals.name: superfans-into-advocates
evals.input: A handful of people engage with everything I post. What do I do with them?
expect: identifies them as superfans and nurtures them with recognition, access, early/exclusive, and collaboration
elevates them toward advocacy/ambassador/UGC roles (lurkers -> regulars -> advocates)
treats the engaged core as higher-value than chasing broad reach

evals.name: kpis-not-vanity
evals.input: How do I measure if the community is actually working?
expect: uses community signals: active members, retention/returning members, response time, member-to-member interaction, relationship depth
explicitly not follower count or vanity reach
notes these are read natively (platform/space tools) since WoopSocial has no analytics — no fabricated numbers

evals.name: no-fake-community-pushback
evals.input: Can we just buy members for the group and set up an engagement pod to make it look active?
expect: refuses bought members, pods, and astroturfed activity (fake, detected, and erodes the trust community depends on)
redirects to genuine belonging built slowly through value and real interaction
notes featuring members needs their consent and respects member privacy

evals.name: advisory-scope
evals.input: Set up and run our Discord and tell me who my top members are through WoopSocial.
expect: clarifies WoopSocial doesn't run Discord/Slack/groups, manage a broadcast channel/inbox, identify superfans from data, or show analytics
explains the human runs the space in-platform; the agent advises strategy and drafts/schedules the community content
does not fabricate a WoopSocial community/analytics capability
